Commentary.Commentary: So, West Indies hold all the cards at the moment in this Test match and it will be a surprise if they go on to lose this match. England have a lot of work to do and need their relatively inexperienced batting line-up to step up and perform better than the first innings. They have around 14 overs to survive before Stumps. Will they be able to go into Day 4 with all their wickets intact? Stay tuned to find out.

The English bowlers, on the other hand, would be disappointed with their performance. Barring Anderson and Stokes, no other pacer was able to make any impact. Anderson ended up with 3 wickets while Stokes finished with 4. Bess was good with a couple of wickets. It is upto the batsmen now to get them out of trouble and rub the trail off without losing many wickets.

End of an excellent innings for the West Indies. They lead by 114 runs and would be very happy with the total. They are dominating this game and are looking favourites going into the third innings. Their batting innings started with Kraigg Brathwaite scoring a well deserved half-century. They certainly lost some wickets in the middle overs but the duo of Roston Chase and Shane Dowrich ensured that they get a good lead. Dowrich managed to reach his fifty and added some useful runs before he was dismissed. Holder, the skipper, failed but they will feel that they have enough lead to put pressure on the English batting.

OUT! LBW! Another on-field call that has been overturned. Chase's patient and very good innings comes to an end. England desperately needed a wicket and they have got it. Once again it is Anderson who has done the damage. He has been the best bowler for England and Stokes so far. Anderson bowls a good length delivery on off, it is bowled at a good pace and nips back in. Chase looks to defend but misses and gets hit around the knee roll of his front pad. The England players put in an appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Anderson, Stokes and Buttler all have a quick chat after which Stokes signals the 'T'. Anderson's foot is fine so we move onto Ultra Edge and there is no spike there. Is height going to be an issue? No, it's not as Ball Tracker comes in and shows all reds as the ball is going on to hit the middle and leg pole. Chase's vigilant knock comes to an end and England get the wicket they were craving for. End of an excellent partnership as well which has taken West Indies in the driver's seat. They lead by 63 runs.

The second new ball is available now and the hosts should take it. They have taken the second new ball and it will be James Anderson who will be using it first up.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

A better session for England but still it is West Indies who are dictating the game. The tourists lead by 31 and still have 5 wickets in hand and with their skipper and the best batter in the team, Jason Holder yet to come, they are in ascendancy. The hosts, on the other hand, showed some fight in this session but faded away towards the end. They will need to find a way and get their morale up and try and restrict the lead to under 100. With the second new ball available straight after Tea, the Three Lions will be very hopeful of doing that. What's in store for us in the final session? Join us at 1615 Local (1515 GMT) to find out.

But if you consider the stats for the wicket-keeper batsmen since 2018 and put in a filter of minimum 500 Test runs, Shane shoots up to the top and dominates the list comprising of BJ Watling, Rishabh Pant, Quinton de Kock and Tim Paine. Well done, silent hero!

But since then he has been very flashy in his approach. In the last 7 innings, five have seen single-digit scores. Is it time for West Indies to look for some other option? Joshua Da Silva could be one who impressed everyone in the final warm-up game with scores of 133* and 56*.

We are back with the action from the second session of Day 3. The England players are making their way out to the middle and are being followed by Shamarh Brooks and Roston Chase. James Anderson will start the proceedings with the ball.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

It was all West Indies on Day 2 and they have dominated the first session of Day 3 as well. A very good batting effort from Brathwaite has seen the tourists score 102 runs in this session and have lost just 2 wickets, with both overnight batsmen back in the hut. The tourists now just trail by 45 runs. England have had a tough game so far and they are clearly chasing this one. They will need to find a way to keep West Indies' lead to a minimum as at this point they are dictating the game. The hosts haven't found it easy as the conditions today have been the best to bat in the three days so far. Can England find a way to impress in this Test post Lunch or will West Indies continue their dominance? Join us for the second session at 1340 Local (1240 GMT) to find out.

We have been greeted with bright sunshine on Day 3 and it is time to get Day 3 underway! The England players make their way out to the middle followed by Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope. Mark Wood will complete his over. Here we go...

A warm welcome to all for Day 3 of the first Test between England and West Indies! Day 2 ended with West Indies taking advantage over England as they first bowled out the hosts for 204 and then their batters started well and have reached 57 for 1, trailing by 147 runs. They have their most experienced batters at the crease in Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope and a lot will depend on them. The English bowlers were not up to the mark and they will want to perform better today to snatch the advantage away from the tourists. Bad light forced early Stumps for two days in a row but the good news is that the weather is predicted to be clear today and we might get a full day's play. 98 overs of action coming your way. What will happen? Will England make a comeback in this game or will the visitors continue to dominate? Stay with us to find out...
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Going into Day 3, West Indies will want their batsmen to keep on batting and try to take the lead. They have an inexperienced batting line-up but they will be eager to do well. England, on the other hand, have a lot of work to do and their bowlers will need to improve. Here's hoping that the rain stays away. An interesting Day 3 awaits us. Join us for that on Friday, 10th July at 1100 Local (1000 GMT). Until then, stay safe and take care.

A very tough day for England. They were out-bowled by the pace, consistency and accuracy of the West Indies' bowlers and now find themselves chasing this game. Their batsmen struggled with the bat earlier in the day and then have found it hard to find the rhythm with the ball. Ben Stokes will hope that his troops can sort themselves out and have a better Day 3. James Anderson was their best bowler but was unlucky. It won't be an easy task as the weather for the next three days is expected to be sunnier than the first two days and it will get easier for batting.

STUMPS ON DAY 2! A much, much better day of cricket but in the end once again, there's a party spoiler and this time it is bad light. West Indies are in the driver's seat in this Test after Day 2 in Southampton clearly belonged to them. Jason Holder led from the front and his 6/42 along with Gabriel's 4-fer bundled out England for just 204. After the bowlers did their job, West Indies managed to start their innings with the willow in strong fashion and at the end of the day trail the hosts by 147 runs with 9 wickets still in hand.

Update 1822 Local (1722 GMT) - Unfortunately, there has been no improvement in the conditions and any further play looks difficult. We fear that Stumps is not far away. No official confirmation yet. Stay tuned for further updates.

The encouraging sign is that the umpires are still on the field but the bad news is that the weather does look a bit gloomy to be honest.

Ball Tracker then comes up and it shows all reds. Finally the umpires get one right and West Indies have lost one of their 3 reviews. Campbell has to finally take the long walk back.
FOUR! Good length ball on middle, Campbell flicks it to the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Good length ball on middle, Campbell looks to defend but it takes the inside edge and onto the pads.
Good length ball on off, John looks to defend but it takes the outside edge which goes towards the second slip fielder.

NOT OUT! Another on-field decision which goes against West Indies has been overturned! The streak of successful reviews for them continues. The ball is going over the stumps. Good length ball outside off, Campbell looks to leave it but it comes in sharply. He gets rapped on the pads and Anderson goes up in appeal. The umpire raises the finger. Campbell goes for the review after discussing it with the third umpire. There is no bat on it confirms the third umpire and the Ball Tracker shows that it is going over the stumps.
John Campbell has taken another review as he has been given out LBW by the umpire. It is straight but it looks like it is a little high. Let's see what happens.
Anderson comes around the wicket to Campbell and bowls a length ball on the pads, Campbell looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. There is a mild appeal for LBW but nothing from the umpire.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Brathwaite flicks it to square leg where the fielder dives to make a good stop.
Shortish delivery on middle, Brathwaite defends it out off the back foot onto the pitch.
On a length on middle, Kraigg defends it out.
Full delivery on middle, John flicks it towards mid on where Wood fumbles allowing the batters to take a single.

EDGED and well fielded! Good length ball on off, John  looks to defend but it takes the outside edge and goes through the gully region. Denly chases after it and makes the stop. Two taken. The umpires check whether it is a clean save and the replays show that it is.
Good length delivery on middle, Campbell looks to flick but gets an inside edge towards mid-wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full delivery on off, Brathwaite defends it out.
Full on middle, Brathwaite plays it back to the bowler.
Fullish delivery down the leg side, Brathwaite looks to flick but misses.
Full on off, Kraigg defends it towards cover.

FOUR LEG BYES! Poor bowling from James Anderson! Good length delivery on the pads, Brathwaite looks to flick but fails to get any bat on it. It brushes his thigh pad and goes past Buttler and into the fine leg fence.
Archer bends his back and bowls a pacy bouncer. It is bowled around middle, and not enough to trouble Campbell as he ducks under it comfortably.
Short on middle, Campbell defends it solidly off the back foot.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Campbell works it to the deep square leg region for a couple.
On a length on off, John defends it off the back foot towards the point region.
BOUNCER! It is bowled around middle, Campbell looks to pull but misses. Buttler hops and collects it.
Excellent yorker but John plays it well! It is bowled around middle by Archer. Campbell manages to defend it towards the mid-wicket region.
On a length on off, Brathwaite defends it to get through the over.
Good length delivery on middle, Brathwaite defends it towards mid-wicket.
Length ball away from the off pole, Brathwaite leaves it alone.
Fuller delivery on middle, Campbell pushes it through mid on. Bess gives it a chase and stops the ball with a slide, taking some grass off the field in the process. Three taken by the batsmen.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Campbell blocks it.
FOUR! Overpitched and Campbell is there to punish it. It is outside off, Campbell is quick to get on his front foot and cream it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
BEATEN! Extra pace from Jofra Archer. Back of a length delivery outside off, Brathwaite hops to defend this one but fails to get any bat on it.
Full delivery outside off, Kraigg pushes it to cover.
Full on off, Brathwaite prods forward and flicks it to the leg side.
Short of a length down the leg side, Kraigg shoulders arms to this one.
Good length ball on off, Kraigg defends it to the cover region.
Archer starts with a length ball on middle, Brathwaite flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a couple.

Good news! The umpires have decided that the play is fit to resume and the players are making their way out to the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell walk followed by the England players. Jofra Archer will start with the ball.

Kemar Roach is up for a chat from a good social distance. Roach says that they are happy to restrict England to around 200 and now it is upto them to bat well. Tells that the plan was to bowl fuller and the nature of the pitch is a bit slow and is happy that it worked for them. Says he felt fantastic with his rhythm. On the pitch, he says there is enough there for the bowlers if you bowl in the right areas and says keeping the shine on one side was hard. On the saliva ban, he says he did it almost a couple of times but is happy not to have done it. Tells that they had to rub the ball hard. Tells that he is the leader of the bowling attack and says they just look to give it their best shot and work hard. On taking a knee before the game, Roach says it was very important and the gesture was heart warming and tells that seeing the English players also taking the knee was heart warming.

The players are off the field. No it is not raining but the umpires are not happy with the light and just like Day 1, Bad Lights has stopped play here. England would not mind this break as the West Indies batsmen have done well so far. There is a possibility that this might be the end of the day's play as well but let's hope that is not the case.

NOT OUT! It is pitching outside leg. Another good review from West Indies, this time from one of their batsmen. Good length ball on middle and leg, Campbell looks to drive but misses and gets hit on the pads. Anderson and the rest appeal and the umpire obliges as he raises the dreaded finger. Campbell has a long thought with his partner Kraigg Brathwaite and decides to review at the last moment. The Ultra Edge shows no bat but the Ball Tracker shows that it is pitching outside leg and Campbell survives. Excellent decision to review and West Indies' streak of successful reviews continues.
Campbell has been given out LBW! After a long decision with Brathwaite, John decides to go for the review. It looks like it has pitched outside leg and the Ball Tracker confirms it.
Length ball on middle, John defends it out off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Good length ball around off, nipping in sharply! Campbell looks to leave but gets hit on the pads as the ball goes to the keeper. The England players go up in huge appeal but the umpire shows no interest. Stokes and Anderson decide against the review. The Ball Tracker shows that it was pitching outside leg. Good decision not to review.
Full delivery outside off, Campbell drives it through the cover region and picks up a couple.
Length ball on off, Kraigg defends it to cover and picks up a single.

An appeal for LBW! Good length ball on middle and leg, Campbell looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. An appeal is made but the umpire shakes his head.  Probably going down the leg side. Ball Tracker confirms that it was going down the leg side.
Length ball on middle, John defends it out.
Good length ball on off, Brathwaite defends it to cover and takes off for a single. The fielder has a shy at the keeper's end but misses. Campbell was in though.

It's a nightmare for batsmen! Overcast conditions, a swing bowler operating from one end, a fiery bowler unleashing from other. Who wants to be an opener? But as the saying goes, hard times reveal your true character and that of those around you. So far, so good from West Indies.
On a length on middle, Kraigg defends it out.
Archer is not finding his line right at the moment! Bowls another one down the leg side, Kraigg leaves it alone.
LEG BYES! Archer bowls a full delivery on the pads, Brathwaite misses out as he fails to get any bat with his flick. The ball brushes his pad and goes to fine leg. The batters take two leg byes.
Good length ball on the pads, Campbell looks to flick but it takes the inside edge and goes towards deep square leg. A couple taken.
Good length ball way outside off, Campbell does not feel the need to play at that one as he leaves it alone.
Anderson dishes another length ball on middle, John solidly defends it to cover.
Outside off, John makes another leave to the keeper.
On a length on middle, Campbell looks to flick but it hits the thigh pad and goes towards gully.
Good length ball on middle, Brathwaite flicks it to mid-wicket for a single.
On a length on middle, Kraigg defends it to cover and takes a quick single.
DID YOU KNOW? James Anderson has dismissed Kraigg Brathwaite 7 times in Test cricket - the most by any bowler. Can Jimmy make it 8?
Archer strays on the pads this time and Brathwaite flicks it to deep square leg for a couple.
Short ball on middle, Brathwaite uncomfortably fends it away to square leg.
Back of a length delivery on middle, John looks to defend but it hits the gloves and rolls to point. A single taken.
Length ball on middle, Campbell defends it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Finds the gap does Campbell! Good length ball outside off, Campbell takes a stride forward and drives it through the vacant gully region for the first boundary of the innings.
Another length ball but is way outside off, Kraigg has no problems in leaving this one alone. Back-to-back maidens from Anderson.
Outside off, left alone by Brathwaite.
On a length on middle, Kraigg defends it out onto the pitch.

BEATEN! Another lovely delivery from James! This one was even better than the previous one! Good length ball around the off stump line, which moves away late. Brathwaite looks to block it but fails to get any bat on it.
The light meter was out before the start of Anderson's over but no issues as of now as it quickly went out as well.
BEATEN! This is what Anderson is known for! Brilliant bowling! Length delivery around off, with some swing away. Brathwaite looks to defend but misses it altogether.
Good length ball outside off, Brathwaite lets the ball go to the keeper.
Length ball on off, Kraigg looks to flick but gets an inside edge which goes towards mid-wicket for a single. Brathwaite is off the mark. 4 from Archer's first over.
BOUNCER! Archer goes short this time and bowls it around middle and leg, Brathwaite does well to duck under it.
Good length ball outside off, left alone by Brathwaite.
Good shot from Campbell! Archer overpitches this one on off, Campbell prods forward and drives it through mid off. Anderson chases after it but cannot stop the batsmen from taking three.
Good length ball outside off, John shoulders arms to this one.
Archer starts with a pacy delivery outside the off stump line, Campbell does not bother to play at that one.
Barbados born, Jofra Archer to partner James Anderson from the other end with the new ball.
A maiden to start from Anderson! Very full delivery outside off, Kraigg plays out this delivery by pushing this towards point. A good start from James. No runs from it.
Anderson dishes a good length ball swinging away, Brathwaite waits and then solidly defends it out.
Another length ball from Anderson which is bowled outside off, Kraigg shoulders arms to this one.
Some swing on offer there! Good length delivery outside off, swinging away from the batsman. Brathwaite watches it carefully and leaves the ball alone.
Good length ball from Anderson around the off stump line, Kraigg is solid in defense as he plays it towards point.
Anderson starts with a back of a length delivery with little to no swing on that ball. Brathwaite defends this one off the back foot towards the point region.
